```{r}

# Create combination sets for isolated two-patch systems. In the previous code we have found combinations of patches that created isolated two-patch systems. However, we would inflate our degrees of freedom if we were to compare all the isolated two-patch systems to the meta-ecosystems. For example, if we were to compare the Small meta-ecosystems to all the Small isolated two-patch systems. This is because isolated two-patch systems would be autocorrelated if they one patch that was the same patch. To get rid of this autocorrelation, in the analysis we will compare six meta-ecosystems to six isolated two-patch systems, where each comparison contains different isolated two-patch systems, where the patches were combined differently. In each comparison we have what we call a "combination set" of isolated two-patch systems. For example, let's say we want to create a combination set for Small isolated systems. Let's supposed that the culture ID of small blue isolated is 1-5 and that the culture of small green is 6-10. Then, a combination set could be: 1|6, 2|7, 3|8, 4|9, 5|10.

# To find such combination sets, I keep the first patch type in numerical order. Then I perform a permutation of the order in which the patches of the second type are arranged. Finally, I combine them. Going back to the example of before, let's say the first patch type is medium blue. Then it will be just 1,2,3,4,5. If the second patch type is medium green, then its permutations will be 6,7,8,9,10 then 6,7,8,10,9 then 6,7,10,8,9 and so on. Finally, I would combine them so that they become: 1|6, 1|7, 1|8, 1|9, 1|10 then 1|6, 1|7, 1|8, 1|10, 1|9 then 1|6, 1|7, 1|10, 1|8, 1|9 and so on.

create.isolated.sets = function(system_type_i) {
  
  ID_green_patches = isolated_two_patch_systems %>%
    filter(system_type == system_type_i) %>%
    pull(green_patch_IDs)
  ID_green_patches = unlist(strsplit(ID_green_patches, ", ")) %>%
    as.double()
  
  ID_blue_patches = isolated_two_patch_systems %>%
    filter(system_type == system_type_i) %>%
    pull(blue_patch_IDs)
  ID_blue_patches = unlist(strsplit(ID_blue_patches, ", ")) %>%
    as.double()
  
  combination_sets_isolated_systems <- data.frame(set = rep(1 : length(permn(ID_blue_patches)),
                                                  each = length(ID_green_patches)),
                                        ID_blue_patches = unlist(flatten(permn(ID_blue_patches))),
                                        ID_green_patches = rep(ID_green_patches, times = length(permn(ID_blue_patches)))) %>%
    mutate(system_type = system_type_i,
           connection = "isolated") %>%
    rename(ID_blue_patch = ID_blue_patches,
           ID_green_patch = ID_green_patches) %>%
    select(system_type,
           connection,
           set,
           ID_blue_patch,
           ID_green_patch) %>%
    filter(
      !ID_blue_patch %in% patches_to_take_off,
      !ID_green_patch %in% patches_to_take_off
    ) %>%
    full_join(
      combinations_isolated_n_metaecos %>%
        filter(system_type == system_type_i)
    )
  
  return(combination_sets_isolated_systems)
  
}
```

```{r}
i = 0
combination_sets_isolated_systems <- list()
for(system_i in unique(combinations_isolated$system_type)){
  
  i = i + 1
  
  combination_sets_isolated_systems[[i]] = create.isolated.sets(system_i)
  
}

combination_sets_isolated_systems = combination_sets_isolated_systems %>%
  bind_rows()
```
